title: Grade 4 SOCIAL STUDIES — Premium Revision Paper #9

pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which direction is Nakuru from Nairobi? (1 mark)
   A. South
   B. North-west
   C. South-east
   D. East

2. Why are cardinal points better than left and right for giving directions? (1 mark)
   A. They only work at night
   B. They do not change when you turn around
   C. They are used only by pilots
   D. They are shorter to say

3. What is a mountain? (1 mark)
   A. A wide flat area
   B. Very high land with steep sides and a peak
   C. A large body of water
   D. A low place between hills

4. Which of these uses the water of a river to make electricity? (1 mark)
   A. A school
   B. A church
   C. A hydroelectric power station
   D. A market

5. If there is no pavement, which side of the road should a pedestrian walk on? (1 mark)
   A. In the middle of the road
   B. The side facing the oncoming traffic
   C. The side with traffic behind
   D. On the side where there is no light

6. How can you keep safe from the sun in the hot season? (1 mark)
   A. Stay in the sun all day
   B. Avoid drinking water
   C. Wear a hat, drink water and rest in the shade
   D. Play in the hottest part of the day

7. During which season do fishermen often dry fish in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Rainy season
   B. Flood season
   C. No season
   D. Dry season

8. Why should a weather chart be filled in at the same time each day? (1 mark)
   A. So that rain stops
   B. So that the chart looks big
   C. So that the sun rises earlier
   D. So that the records can be compared fairly

9. How is money useful in trade? (1 mark)
   A. It grows crops
   B. It makes buying and selling easier
   C. It builds houses
   D. It stops trade

10. Which of these is a service? (1 mark)
   A. A pair of shoes
   B. Treatment by a nurse
   C. A book
   D. A bag of maize

11. Which place is used mainly for prayers and worship? (1 mark)
   A. Hospital
   B. Market
   C. Church, mosque or temple
   D. Factory

12. Which pattern describes houses standing close together around a trading centre? (1 mark)
   A. Linear
   B. Clustered
   C. Empty
   D. Scattered

13. On a dot map where one dot means 1,000 people, an area has 7 dots. How many people live there? (1 mark)
   A. 70
   B. 700
   C. 7,000
   D. 70,000

14. Which area is most likely to be sparsely populated? (1 mark)
   A. A very dry area with little rain
   B. A busy town
   C. A lakeshore with fish
   D. A fertile highland

15. How can a school show traditional culture? (1 mark)
   A. By closing the library
   B. By holding a culture day with songs and dances
   C. By locking classrooms
   D. By stopping all games

16. Why is traditional culture important? (1 mark)
   A. It stops all change
   B. It makes people fight
   C. It gives identity and teaches values
   D. It has no use

17. What is a timeline? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of ruler
   B. A picture of a school
   C. A line showing events in the order they happened
   D. A weather chart

18. What are values? (1 mark)
   A. Types of buildings
   B. Good beliefs that guide our behaviour
   C. Kinds of food
   D. Kinds of money

19. Where is soda ash taken from in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Lake Magadi
   B. Mount Kenya
   C. Kisumu Port
   D. Lake Victoria

20. What is an industry? (1 mark)
   A. A school subject
   B. A place where raw materials are made into goods or a service is given at large scale
   C. A kind of farm animal
   D. A type of weather

21. What is the raw material for sugar? (1 mark)
   A. Wheat
   B. Sugarcane
   C. Tea leaves
   D. Milk

22. Which industry uses milk as raw material? (1 mark)
   A. A shoe workshop
   B. A sugar mill
   C. A cement plant
   D. A dairy

23. Which of these is a jua kali product? (1 mark)
   A. A metal door made in a small workshop
   B. A jet plane
   C. A satellite
   D. A big ship

24. What is a project? (1 mark)
   A. A type of shoe
   B. A plan of work with a start, a finish and a goal
   C. A holiday
   D. A kind of fruit

25. Why is teamwork important in a project? (1 mark)
   A. It makes work harder
   B. It shares work and helps the project succeed
   C. It makes the project fail
   D. It stops others helping

26. A group spent Ksh 400 and earned Ksh 700. What is the profit? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 400
   B. Ksh 300
   C. Ksh 1,100
   D. Ksh 700

27. What does punctuality mean? (1 mark)
   A. Running fast
   B. Arriving late
   C. Speaking loudly
   D. Arriving on time

28. What should you do if you are very angry? (1 mark)
   A. Shout insults
   B. Walk away and calm down
   C. Break something
   D. Hit someone

29. Which of these promotes peace? (1 mark)
   A. Rumours
   B. Sharing
   C. Bullying
   D. Fighting

30. What is a peace garden? (1 mark)
   A. A car park
   B. A market
   C. A place for fighting
   D. A garden where pupils can sit and be calm

31. Which is a responsibility of a child? (1 mark)
   A. Skip school
   B. Respect others and study hard
   C. Steal
   D. Bully others

32. Which of these is a trusted adult? (1 mark)
   A. A person who threatens you
   B. A parent or teacher
   C. A stranger you met online
   D. A person who gives you sweets in secret

33. Which action helps a child with special needs? (1 mark)
   A. Laughing at them
   B. Hiding them
   C. Neglecting them
   D. Including them in games

34. Who writes down what is discussed and decided at a meeting? (1 mark)
   A. The president
   B. The Speaker
   C. The secretary
   D. The patron

35. Which activity can show leadership qualities in class? (1 mark)
   A. Sleeping
   B. Role-playing an elder settling a quarrel
   C. Fighting
   D. Copying

36. What is a clan? (1 mark)
   A. A large family group with a common ancestor
   B. A kind of road
   C. A school
   D. A market

37. Who is a good resource person to learn about community leadership? (1 mark)
   A. A stranger who knows nothing
   B. A village elder
   C. A random shop
   D. A cartoon

38. How many MCAs does each ward elect? (1 mark)
   A. None
   B. Fifty
   C. One
   D. Ten

39. Who is the head of a county government? (1 mark)
   A. The MCA
   B. The Governor
   C. The chief
   D. The Speaker

40. Which of these tasks belongs to the county government? (1 mark)
   A. County roads
   B. Immigration
   C. Foreign affairs
   D. National defence

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give four qualities of a good pupil leader. (4 marks)

42. Explain how a village elder can help two neighbours who quarrel about a fence. (4 marks)

43. Explain what neighbouring counties are. (2 marks)

44. What is the difference between a lake and a river? (2 marks)

45. Describe three problems that crowded areas can have and one way of reducing each. (5 marks)

46. Using time words, write a short history of a school that opened in 1985 and built a library in 2000. (3 marks)

47. Write a short note to invite a resource person to talk about a historic place in your county. Include the reason and the date. (5 marks)

48. Explain the difference between a ceremony and a festival and give one example of each. (4 marks)

49. Explain the meaning of democracy. (2 marks)

50. Describe the houses of two communities in Kenya. (4 marks)

51. Write a short motto for a school and say what it means. (3 marks)

52. Explain what a child should do if someone makes them feel unsafe. (3 marks)

53. Explain what jua kali workers do and why they are important. (4 marks)

54. Explain why the county assembly must check the work of the governor. (5 marks)

55. Explain three elements of democracy and give an example of each in school. (5 marks)

56. Give three questions to ask when choosing a school enterprise project. (3 marks)

57. State two things a good map key should show. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — North-west
   Nakuru is north-west of Nairobi.

2. B — They do not change when you turn around
   Left and right change with the way you face, but north, east, south and west stay the same.

3. B — Very high land with steep sides and a peak
   A mountain is much higher than the land around it.

4. C — A hydroelectric power station
   Hydroelectric stations use falling river water to make electricity.

5. B — The side facing the oncoming traffic
   Facing traffic lets you see vehicles coming towards you.

6. C — Wear a hat, drink water and rest in the shade
   These habits protect us from heat.

7. D — Dry season
   Dry sunny days are best for drying fish.

8. D — So that the records can be compared fairly
   Observing at the same time gives fair comparisons.

9. B — It makes buying and selling easier
   Money is a common way of paying for goods and services.

10. B — Treatment by a nurse
   A service is work done for someone. The others are goods.

11. C — Church, mosque or temple
   Places of worship are for prayer.

12. B — Clustered
   Clustered means close together in a group.

13. C — 7,000
   7 x 1,000 = 7,000.

14. A — A very dry area with little rain
   Dry areas make farming and water supply hard.

15. B — By holding a culture day with songs and dances
   A culture day lets pupils share their heritage.

16. C — It gives identity and teaches values
   Culture helps us to know who we are.

17. C — A line showing events in the order they happened
   A timeline shows events in order.

18. B — Good beliefs that guide our behaviour
   Values guide how we behave.

19. A — Lake Magadi
   Soda ash is mined at Lake Magadi.

20. B — A place where raw materials are made into goods or a service is given at large scale
   Industries change raw materials into products or provide services.

21. B — Sugarcane
   Sugar is made from sugarcane.

22. D — A dairy
   Dairies process milk.

23. A — A metal door made in a small workshop
   Jua kali workers make goods like doors and furniture.

24. B — A plan of work with a start, a finish and a goal
   A project is planned work for a goal.

25. B — It shares work and helps the project succeed
   Sharing roles makes work easier.

26. B — Ksh 300
   700 - 400 = 300.

27. D — Arriving on time
   Punctual people arrive on time.

28. B — Walk away and calm down
   Cooling down prevents harm.

29. B — Sharing
   Sharing builds trust and friendship.

30. D — A garden where pupils can sit and be calm
   A peace garden is calm and beautiful.

31. B — Respect others and study hard
   Rights come with responsibilities.

32. B — A parent or teacher
   Trusted adults protect children.

33. D — Including them in games
   Children with special needs have equal rights.

34. C — The secretary
   The secretary keeps the minutes.

35. B — Role-playing an elder settling a quarrel
   Role play shows how leaders act.

36. A — A large family group with a common ancestor
   A clan traces its origin to one ancestor.

37. B — A village elder
   A village elder knows leadership.

38. C — One
   Each ward elects one MCA.

39. B — The Governor
   The governor leads the county.

40. A — County roads
   County roads belong to the county.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Honest, fair, responsible and a good listener. Accept humble or hard working.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each quality.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Listen to both, be fair, help them to talk and agree, and encourage them to forgive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Neighbouring counties are counties that share a boundary with your county.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sharing a boundary, 1 mark for saying they are next to yours.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: A lake is a large area of water with land around it. A river is water flowing along a channel to a lake or ocean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: Shortage of houses: build more houses. Litter: organise cleaning and waste collection. Traffic: improve roads and public transport. Award marks for each problem and each solution.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each problem/solution pair, up to 5 marks.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: The school was opened in 1985. Later, in 2000, a library was built. Today, pupils read books in the library.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dates, 1 mark for order, 1 mark for time words.

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: A polite greeting, the name of the person, the reason for the invitation, the date and time, and a thank-you at the end.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of the five parts.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: A ceremony marks a special event in life, such as a wedding. A festival is a big celebration with many people, such as the Lamu Cultural Festival.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each example.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Democracy is rule by the people, where everyone has a say in choosing leaders and making decisions.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rule by the people, 1 mark for having a say.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: The Maasai build low houses of wooden frames covered with mud and dung inside a fence called a manyatta. Old coastal houses in Lamu were built of coral stone with carved doors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each community and 1 mark for each description.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Work hard, be kind. It means pupils should study well and be kind to others.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a short motto, 1 mark for its meaning, 1 mark for showing action.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say no loudly, go to a safe place, and tell a trusted adult.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: They make and repair goods such as furniture and metal doors in small workshops. They give jobs, provide cheap goods, and train young people in skills.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: To make sure county money is used honestly, to prevent misuse of power, to make sure services reach people, to protect citizens' interests, and to keep the governor accountable.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.

55. (5 marks)
   Answer: Equality: one vote each. Freedom of expression: giving opinions in class. Majority rule: choosing a game by most votes. Award marks for each element and example.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct element with example, up to 5.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do people want it? Do we have the materials and skills? Is it safe? Can we earn more than we spend?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible question.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: The meaning of the colours and the meaning of the lines or symbols used on the map.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct item.
